title: Hassert: Hardware Assertion-Based Verification Framework with FPGA Acceleration
problem: Hardware verification using software simulators is time-consuming, especially for large benchmarks with assertion-based verification. FPGA prototyping provides speed but lacks fine-grained debugging capabilities when errors occur.
motivation: Hardware verification is a critical bottleneck in chip development, and improving verification speed and debugging capability enables faster and more reliable chip design cycles.
method: Hassert speeds up hardware verification by running automated checks (called assertions) on FPGA hardware instead of in slow software simulation. FPGA is a reconfigurable chip that can be configured to match the hardware design being tested, so these checks run much faster than simulating everything in software. The framework preserves detailed debugging information throughout, so when a check fails, engineers can pinpoint exactly which microarchitecture behavior was incorrect.
key_novelty: Hassert combines assertion-based verification checks with FPGA acceleration while maintaining the debugging visibility that software simulation provides.
contributions: Hassert framework combining ABV with FPGA acceleration for hardware verification
Fine-grained debugging support for FPGA-based verification
Significant speedup over software simulator assertion checking
Automated detection of microarchitecture violations at FPGA speeds
